mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue edging upward while RESIDENTIAL stays flat or slips, weekday trips will convert into retail visits within four weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC above the prior four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increasing for at least two consecutive weeks and RESIDENTIAL not increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT below its recent four-week average will suppress discretionary city-center trips first, so RETAIL_REC will fall within one to two weeks even if WORKPLACES remains near current levels.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls > 3 points week-on-week from the current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days after TRANSIT drops sharply, with no compensating rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rebounds from a dip and stays above its prior week level, warm-weather leisure trips spill into nearby shopping and dining, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks after a recent trough
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week average across the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while RETAIL_REC lags, households are reallocating trips toward necessity shopping, which will keep discretionary retail mobility subdued over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above its current level for two straight weeks while RETAIL_REC does not recover
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals synchronized commuting and public movement; that interaction should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks as after-work shopping and lunch trips recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together for at least one full week.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT stays depressed, people are substituting home-based routines for outings, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and TRANSIT stays materially below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in WORKPLACES mobility beyond the recent plateau indicates easing access and fewer frictions; retail mobility should follow with a one-week lag as consumers combine errands with commuting.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 5 points from its current weekly mean
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by 5 points or more but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both firm up at the same time, weekend and neighborhood trip intensity is broadening, which should support a higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM each turn up for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM rise for two weeks, but RETAIL_REC stays below its prior four-week mean over the following 28 days.
